rationales: A prepared solution is developed through planning, so it is not the unplanned solution described.
A candid solution is not reached through a proper algorithm or work plan.
A strategic solution is based on planned steps, so it does not fit.
A best solution is selected after considering possible solutions, rather than being an unplanned one.
Start marks the beginning of an algorithm, not its termination.
Set is not the termination point of an algorithm.
Goto transfers control to another step rather than terminating the algorithm.
Stop marks the termination point of an algorithm.
A Boolean proposition is a statement evaluated as true or false, not the grammatical category indicated here.
“It is old maid” assigns a property to a subject, making it a categorical proposition.
A moral proposition concerns moral judgments, which this statement does not express.
The statement fits the category of a categorical proposition, so this option is incorrect.
